subject: ClearPay production: sudden latency & throughput gap — urgent contingency request
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops@clearpay.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike — reserved capacity impacted

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a spike in end-to-end latency around 08:00 PST and by 08:05 our downstream errors began to climb. Requests to the /v1/chat endpoint for model variant r-instruct-3b-quant are returning 502s and time-to-first-token is up ~4.4x. This is affecting our checkout flows; current error rate for the last 5m is 1.7% (baseline ~0.1%).

We've attached a short capture (capture-20261121-0810.json) and a Grafana snapshot. Can you confirm whether our reserved throughput is being throttled or if there's a pool saturation event? We need an ETA on mitigation — ClearPay has a 99.9% latency SLA and the SRE team is on standby.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
SRE Lead, ClearPay

Attachments: capture-20261121-0810.json (json request traces), clearpay-grafana-snap.png (png)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — reserved capacity impacted

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm escalating immediately to ops and capacity engineering. A few quick asks that will help us triage faster:

- Can you paste two example request IDs from the capture (X-Request-ID header) and the timestamps (UTC) for 08:02–08:10?
- Confirm whether you've observed an increase in concurrent sessions or a specific job that correlates with the spike.
- Is this traffic routed to our dedicated pool (your contract RDW-3491) or are there fallbacks to hosted instances?

We're running an initial check of your reserved pool headroom and KV cache hit rates. I've attached the first-run diagnostics and the relevant runbook excerpt (runbook-dedicated-burst.pdf). Marissa / Aditya — can you take point on scaling burst capacity and enabling the model fallback to r-instruct-3b-quant-lite if we detect sustained loss of throughput?

I'll follow up within 30 minutes with status.

—Kimberly
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-dedicated-burst.pdf (excerpt)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearpay.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Escalation: ClearPay reserved pool headroom and burst play

Marissa / Aditya — internal ops note. Summary from external: 08:00–08:10 latency spike, 502s, errors up to 1.7%. ClearPay is on reserved capacity (RDW-3491). Initial diagnostics:

- Reserved pool for ClearPay shows queue depth rising and continuous batching windows stretched; effective throughput is down ~28% vs committed baseline.
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 84% to 39% coincident with the spike; suspect cache invalidation or hot-prefix churn.
- No immediate infra alarm (no host OOM), looks like headroom exhaustion + scheduling latencies on shared nodes causing throughput cliffs.

Immediate action items (please confirm completion):
1) Apply emergency burst capacity for ClearPay (enable reserved->burst mapping) and temporarily prioritize their queue (Aditya).
2) If burst is insufficient within 10m, flip model fallback to r-instruct-3b-quant-lite with reduced sequence lengths (Aditya).
3) Investigate cache churn root cause and, if safe, temporarily increase cache retention for ClearPay's namespace (Marissa).
4) Prepare customer-facing note with ETA and compensation options (Kimberly/Marissa).

Attach: initial metric snapshots and trace link: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/ClearPay/latency-dashboard?orgId=1

Please reply-all with status updates.

—Kimberly

(Quoted for context)

Kimberly / Aditya — bringing this to exec visibility. Quick points:

- Priority: ClearPay is a strategic mid-market account with expansion in contract negotiations; SLA impact risks renewal timing.
- Ask: Ops needs to propose an ETA (minutes) for full recovery and a short window for continued monitoring. If recovery > 2 hours, we should offer a one-time credit and schedule a follow-up architecture review.

Aditya: please provide the following by 12:00 PST so I can brief the leadership:
- Current throughput gap (rps) vs committed throughput
- Estimated time to restore via burst + fallback
- Any blockers requiring infra intervention or rebalancing across regions

Kimberly: draft a customer note with the immediate mitigation steps and expected ETA so Samantha has something to share with her SRE team.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success

Thanks team — update from our side: after your initial burst enable at ~09:05 latency dropped and error rate fell to ~0.6%, but over the last hour error rate has trended back up to ~0.8%. We can confirm the requests in the capture: ids 81b9fa2, 81b9fa9 (UTC 16:02:10Z / 16:07:54Z).

We absolutely appreciate the quick triage. Can you confirm next steps and final ETA for either full recovery or a permanent fallback until we complete the follow-up architecture review? Also please confirm whether this incident will be logged in HubSpot (HS-23472) and whether there is an in-flight credit decision.

-Samantha
SRE Lead, ClearPay
